param.label: Number of CPU stressors
param.help: Start N workers that exercise the CPU by computing sqrt(rand()). Use 0 to run on all online CPUs. Leave empty to skip.

param.label: CPU load percentage
param.help: Load the CPU(s) by P percent. 0 means sleep (idle), 100 means full load. Lower values reduce heat and power consumption.

param.label: Number of disk I/O stressors
param.help: Start N workers that exercise the hard drive by writing and deleting temporary files. These produce significant disk activity.

param.label: Number of I/O stressors
param.help: Start N workers that exercise I/O by calling sync(). These stress the system's I/O subsystem.

param.label: Number of virtual memory stressors
param.help: Start N workers that exercise virtual memory by allocating and freeing memory regions.

param.label: Memory per VM stressor
param.help: Amount of memory to allocate per virtual memory worker. Accepts sizes like 256M, 1G, or a percentage of total memory (e.g. 80%). Default is 256 MB per worker.

param.label: Show performance metrics
param.help: Print a summary of bogo-operations per second for each stressor at the end of the run. Useful for comparing performance across runs.

param.label: Number of random stressors
param.help: Start N randomly selected stressors from all available stressor types.

param.label: Run duration
param.help: Stop the stress test after the specified time. Format: a number followed by s (seconds), m (minutes), or h (hours). Default is 10 seconds.

param.label: Run all stressors
param.help: Start N instances of every available stressor. Use -1 to run one instance per online CPU. Warning: this is very resource-intensive.

param.label: Stressor class
param.help: Restrict stressors to a specific class (e.g. cpu, io, vm, network, filesystem). Use with the 'Sequential' option to run all stressors in that class one by one.

param.label: Number of random stressors
param.help: Start N randomly selected stressors from all available stressor types.

param.label: Sequential run count
param.help: Run all stressors one by one, each for the duration specified in 'Run duration'. N is the number of instances of each stressor running concurrently. Use -1 to match the number of online CPUs.

param.label: CPU affinity
param.help: Pin stressors to specific CPUs. Format: comma-separated CPU numbers and ranges, e.g. '0,2-4,6'. Useful for testing specific cores.

param.label: Run duration
param.help: Stop after the specified time. Format: number + s/m/h (e.g. 30s, 5m, 1h). Default: 10 seconds.

param.label: Exclude stressors
param.help: Comma-separated list of stressor names to exclude from the run (e.g. 'hdd,numa,mmapfork'). Useful when --all or --random triggers stressors that cause problems.

param.label: Aggressive mode
param.help: Enable the most demanding options for each stressor (larger memory allocations, more file handles, etc.). Produces maximum load.

param.label: Maximize resource usage
param.help: Push each stressor to use the maximum available resources (memory, file space, etc.). Use with caution on production systems.

param.label: Show performance metrics
param.help: Print a detailed summary of bogo-operations per second for each stressor.

param.label: Brief metrics
param.help: Print only the non-zero bogo-operations per second metrics. Less verbose than full metrics.

param.label: Show timing statistics
param.help: Display overall time utilisation statistics at the end of the run, including user/system time and load averages.

param.label: CPU stressors
param.help: Start N workers that exercise the CPU by computing sqrt(rand()). Use 0 for all online CPUs.

param.label: CPU operations limit
param.help: Stop each CPU stressor after N bogo-operations instead of waiting for the timeout. Useful for short, controlled runs.

param.label: CPU load percentage
param.help: Load the CPU(s) by P percent. 0 = sleep, 100 = full load. Allows throttling CPU usage.

param.label: CPU stress method
param.help: Select the computation method used by the CPU stressors. Different methods stress different arithmetic operations.

param.label: Cyclic latency stressors
param.help: Start N workers that measure real-time scheduling latencies. Requires the CAP_SYS_NICE capability for accurate results.

param.label: Cyclic measurement method
param.help: Method used to sleep between cyclic latency measurements.

param.label: Cyclic latency distribution interval
param.help: Interval in nanoseconds for the latency distribution histogram. E.g. 2500 means histogram buckets of 2500 ns each.

param.label: Cyclic scheduling priority
param.help: Real-time scheduling priority for the cyclic stressor. Range 1-100. Higher values get more CPU time. Requires CAP_SYS_NICE.

param.label: Cyclic sleep interval (nanoseconds)
param.help: Sleep duration in nanoseconds between cyclic latency measurements. E.g. 10000 = 10 microseconds.

param.label: Fork stressors
param.help: Start N workers that rapidly create (fork) and reap child processes. Tests process creation and destruction performance.

param.label: Disk I/O stressors
param.help: Start N workers that write and delete temporary files on the hard drive. Produces significant disk activity.

param.label: I/O sync stressors
param.help: Start N workers that call sync() to flush filesystem buffers. Stresses the I/O subsystem and kernel.

param.label: Mixed I/O stressors
param.help: Start N workers that perform a mix of read, write, and seek operations on temporary files. More realistic I/O workload than --io or --hdd alone.

param.label: I/O mix file size
param.help: Total size of the temporary files used by the iomix stressors. Accepts sizes like 10M, 1G, or a percentage of free disk space (e.g. 10%).

param.label: Virtual memory stressors
param.help: Start N workers that allocate and free memory regions, stressing the virtual memory subsystem.

param.label: Memory per VM stressor
param.help: Amount of memory to allocate per virtual memory worker. Accepts sizes like 256M, 1G, or a percentage of total memory (e.g. 80%). Default: 256 MB.

tool.help:
**stress-ng** — Stress test a computer system in various selectable ways
stress-ng was originally intended to make a machine work hard and trip hardware issues such as thermal overruns as well as operating system bugs that only occur when a system is being thrashed hard. Use stress-ng with caution as some of the tests can make a system run hot on poorly designed hardware and also can cause excessive system thrashing which may be difficult to stop.
stress-ng can also measure test throughput rates; this can be useful to observe performance changes across different operating system releases or types of hardware. However, it has never been intended to be used as a precise benchmark test suite, so do **not** use it in this manner.
-----
**Common options** provides quick access to the most frequently used stressors (CPU, disk, I/O, virtual memory) with sensible defaults.
**All options** exposes the full set of stressors and control parameters, including the ability to run all stressors, run them sequentially, filter by class, pin to specific CPUs, and more.
**Run duration** controls how long the test runs. Start with short durations (e.g. 10 seconds) to verify your system handles the load before running longer tests.
**Bogo-operations** are a stress-ng concept: each stressor defines its own unit of work (a "bogo-operation"). The `--metrics` flag reports how many bogo-operations per second each stressor achieved, which can be useful for relative performance comparisons.
-----
**Examples**
`--cpu 4 --io 2 --vm 1 --vm-bytes 1G --timeout 60s` Run for 60 seconds with 4 CPU stressors, 2 I/O stressors, and 1 VM stressor using 1 GB of memory.
`--vm 8 --vm-bytes 80% --timeout 1h` Run 8 virtual memory stressors that combined use 80% of available memory for 1 hour. Each stressor uses 10% of available memory.
`--sequential 2 --timeout 2m --metrics` Run 2 simultaneous instances of all stressors sequentially (one by one), each for 2 minutes, and summarise with performance metrics at the end.
`--cpu 4 --cpu-method fft --cpu-ops 10000 --metrics-brief` Run 4 FFT CPU stressors, stop after 10000 bogo-operations, and produce a brief metrics summary.
`--all 4 --timeout 5m` Run 4 instances of all stressors for 5 minutes. **Warning: very resource-intensive.**
`--random 32 --exclude numa,hdd,key` Run 32 randomly selected stressors, excluding the numa, hdd, and key stressors.
Project: https://github.com/ColinIanKing/stress-ng
